chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil and 'Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn Humran, all together from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
The minimum amount for which the thief's hand is cut off is one-fifth of a dinar.

key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief who commits theft meeting the legal conditions
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: a dinar, a gold coin used here as a measure of legal value
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: the prescribed cutting off carried out as a legal hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of theft for which the thief's hand is cut off in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the minimum threshold of stolen property that incurs the hadd punishment for theft. It is a jurisprudential report used in discussions of judicial rulings concerning theft and the legal conditions for implementing the prescribed penalty.
